ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=974792d4cdda introduced a bulk import job (bulk_import_job.ex) that runs at startup and acquires 20 of the 30 available DB connections from the shared postgres-primary pool to execute 1420 batched UPSERT statements against the cart_items table. The migration added in 20260505_add_bulk_import_upsert.sql performs ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE without a covering index on (user_id, product_id), causing full sequential scans and table-level lock escalation on every batch. During peak traffic this starves cart-service of DB connections, triggers deadlocks between the import and live user queries, exhausts the connection pool, and causes cascading 503/500 errors across all cart endpoints.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately kill the running bulk import job (bulk-2026-05-05-0543) via the job scheduler to release the 20 held DB connections and restore cart-service availability. 2. Add a unique index on cart_items(user_id, product_id) to support the ON CONFLICT clause and eliminate sequential scans: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_cart_items_user_product ON cart_items(user_id, product_id);` 3. Reschedule the bulk import job to run during off-peak hours (e.g., 02:00–04:00 UTC) with connection pool limits capped at 5 connections and batch sizes reduced to 20 rows. 4. If the index cannot be added within the maintenance window, roll back sha=974792d4cdda by reverting bulk_import_job.ex and the migration, then redeploy.
